headline: Profit swings positive as writedown fades, margins compress
summary_short: Crocs' Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 2.6% y/y to $1,179M, but net income swung to $205M ($4.13 diluted EPS) from a $492M net loss a year earlier as a non-recurring HEYDUDE trademark/goodwill impairment did not repeat; gross margin fell 230bp to 59.4% on tariff duties.
summary_long: Revenue rose 2.6% y/y to $1,179M on higher constant-currency ASP (+3.3%) in both brands, partly offset by lower HEYDUDE volume — Crocs Brand revenue grew 4.3% while HEYDUDE fell 5.7%. Gross margin fell 230bp to 59.4% on incremental tariff duties and unfavorable Crocs Brand mix, partly offset by lower product costs. SG&A rose to $415.0M (35.2% of revenue) on DTC investment. Operating income jumped to $285.7M and net income to $204.9M ($4.13 diluted EPS) from a $492.3M net loss, as a $738.1M HEYDUDE trademark/goodwill impairment recorded a year ago did not recur. Cash was $170.3M; the company bought back $250.6M of stock and lifted its buyback authorization by $1.5B in July. No forward guidance appears in this 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: The swing to profitability is driven almost entirely by the non-recurrence of a $738.1M HEYDUDE trademark and goodwill impairment recorded in Q2 FY2025, not by underlying operating improvement.
Higher constant-currency ASP in both brands (+$37.9M) and favorable FX (+$6.3M) drove the increase, partly offset by lower HEYDUDE unit volume (-$14.1M).
Gross margin fell 230bp y/y primarily on unfavorable duties from incremental tariffs for both brands and unfavorable Crocs Brand product mix, partly offset by lower Crocs Brand product costs.
Rose alongside the tariff-driven duty increases affecting both brands, partly offset by lower Crocs Brand product costs.
Swung from a loss because last year's quarter carried the one-time HEYDUDE trademark and goodwill impairment; this year had no equivalent charge.
Mirrors the operating-income swing — no repeat of last year's HEYDUDE impairment charge, partly offset by higher SG&A from DTC channel investment.
Diluted EPS growth outpaces net income growth because weighted diluted shares fell 11.0% y/y as the company repurchased stock.
Reflects the company's ongoing buyback program — $250.6M of common stock repurchased this quarter alone.
Cash fell y/y as $250.6M of quarterly share repurchases and capex outpaced operating cash generation, even as operating cash flow itself improved.
